# dbd — Database Designer

> A standalone CLI and embeddable Rust library for managing database schemas as code.

dbd parses SQL DDL files, resolves dependencies, generates migrations, loads data, and deploys to PostgreSQL, Supabase, SQLite, or Convex — all from a single binary with zero runtime dependencies.

## Core concept

SQL files are the source of truth. Path = `ddl/<type>/<schema>/<name>.<ext>` (roles have no schema): `<type>` ∈ table|view|materialized_view|function|procedure|enum|role, ext `.ddl`|`.sql`. Folder = type, parent = schema, filename = entity name. Singular type folder is canonical (plural accepted but `dbd doctor --fix` migrates it to singular).
- `ddl/table/config/lookups.ddl` → entity `config.lookups` (table)
- `ddl/view/config/genders.ddl` → entity `config.genders` (view)
- `ddl/materialized_view/analytics/daily_sales.ddl` → entity `analytics.daily_sales` (materialized view; write `create materialized view if not exists …` + trailing `create [unique] index …`)
- `ddl/procedure/staging/import_lookups.ddl` → entity `staging.import_lookups` (procedure)

Files are parsed once into a rich internal representation (Entity + TableDef). That same structure drives every feature: dependency graph, apply, migrations, DBML generation, data import.

## design.yaml structure

```yaml
project:
  name: MyProject

source:
  dialect: postgresql

target:
  postgres:
    url: $DATABASE_URL
    extensions: [uuid-ossp]
    roles:
      - name: app_user
    skip_schemas: [auth]       # target owns these schemas — exclude their entities from the design

schemas: [config, staging]

import:
  staging: [staging]
  options: { truncate: true, format: csv }

export:
  - config.lookups

materialized_views:            # refresh scheduling for ddl/materialized_view/ entities (pg_cron)
  options:                     # shared defaults for every matview
    refresh: "0 2 * * *"       # cron expression; omit ⇒ no scheduled refresh
    concurrently: true         # needs a unique index on the matview
  overrides:                   # per-matview overrides (by qualified name)
    analytics.top_products: { refresh: "*/30 * * * *" }

dbml:
  base:
    exclude: { schemas: [staging] }
  core:
    include: { schemas: [config] }
    output: core.dbml          # filename (default: <key>.dbml)
    auto_group_by_schema: true # emit `TableGroup <schema>` per schema
    groups:                    # or explicit groups (precedence over auto)
      - name: lookups
        tables: [config.lookups, config.lookup_values]

scopes:                        # named entity subsets — deploy one design to many DBs
  hub:
    includes: [config, app.users]   # schema | schema.entity | schema.* (wildcard)
    deps: report               # report (default, errors on gaps) | include (auto-closure)
    extensions: []             # optional per-scope allowlist; omit=all, []=none, [vector]=subset
  reporting:
    excludes: [staging.*]      # wildcard drops a schema's entities but keeps the schema

ignore: [bfs, my_company.*]
```

Scopes are orthogonal to `target` (DB platform) and the connection: pair them at run time with `dbd deploy --scope hub --database $HUB_URL`. `includes`/`excludes` items are a bare schema (its entities + the schema entity), a qualified `schema.entity`, or a `schema.*` wildcard (same `prefix.*` syntax as `ignore:`; drops a schema's entities while keeping the schema — for `includes`, `schema.*` ≡ `schema`). A dependency gap (in-scope entity referencing a managed entity outside the scope) is an error under `report`; `external:` entities are never gaps. An optional per-scope `extensions:` allowlist restricts which `target.extensions` apply (omit ⇒ all, `[]` ⇒ none, `[vector]` ⇒ subset) — for deploying to a DB that lacks an extension; roles/externals stay always-on. Omit `default`/the block ⇒ full set.

## Commands

- `dbd init` — scaffold project; or **reverse-engineer** a whole project + baseline snapshot from an existing source: `--from-db <conn>` (live DB) or `--from-dbml <file>` (DBML, mutually exclusive). Refuses against a dbd-managed DB (use `merge`) or an existing `design.yaml`. Flags: `--schema`/`--exclude-schema`/`--all-schemas`/`--roles`/`--version`/`--dry-run`; secrets stay out (`$DATABASE_URL`)
- `dbd merge` — sync a DB (or `--from-dbml <file>`) into the current project (reverse-engineer + reconcile, never edits `design.yaml`): foreign or managed `D≥Y` → overwrite DDL + auto-snapshot the diff; managed `D<Y` → refuse (stale DB, no override); orphans reported never deleted; same selection flags as init
- `dbd inspect` — validate, report errors/warnings (+ scope dependency gaps with `--scope`); `--fix` auto-formats DDL files in place; `--from-db` resolves references against the live catalog (uses `-d`/`--database`) and caches to `.dbd/refcache.json`. Surfaces unresolved migration `-- TODO:`s
- `dbd apply` — apply schemas + entities + pending migrations (blocks while migration TODOs remain); `--with-policies` also applies RLS
- `dbd import` — load staging data (CSV/TSV/JSONL) from the `import/` convention; env-specific files under `import/<env>/<schema>/` load only when `-e <env>` matches. `-n <table> -f <file>` loads one explicit file (format from extension)
- `dbd export` — export table data (scope-aware) to `export/<schema>/<name>.<fmt>`; `-f/--format` sets the format, `-o/--output <dir>` the destination dir (`<dir>/<name>.<fmt>`, e.g. straight into `import/` for a round-trip)
- `dbd refresh` — run `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW [CONCURRENTLY]` now (honoring each matview's resolved `concurrently`); `-n <entity>` or `-n <schema>.*` targets a subset, omit for all. Scheduled refresh is otherwise managed in-database via pg_cron (jobs named `dbd:refresh:<schema>.<name>`, synced on `apply`/`deploy`; needs the `pg_cron` extension)
- `dbd deploy --source owner/repo/path` — fetch + apply + import from GitHub; GitHub sources cache under `~/.cache/dbd` — `--no-cache` re-downloads this source, `--clear-cache` wipes the whole cache first
- `dbd reconcile` — pre-release (pre-v1) **declarative** apply: diff the live DB against the design and apply `CREATE`/`ALTER` in place, no snapshots/version bump; scoped to managed schemas. `--allow-destructive` drops columns/constraints on managed tables; `--prune` drops orphaned tables (in a managed schema, gone from the design); orphaned enums are only warned. Materialized views: create-if-absent (stamped with a `dbd:hash` sentinel comment); a drifted definition is only **warned**, never auto-dropped (a matview recreate is `DROP … CASCADE`, losing data/dependents — drop it manually, then `apply`/reconcile recreates it). Disabled once `project.released`
- `dbd diff` — read-only: show the complete live-DB↔design difference (columns, PK/unique, FK, CHECK, indexes, column comments, enums) plus **materialized-view drift** (each matview reported `missing`/`drifted`/`unstamped`/`orphan` via its `dbd:hash` sentinel; counts toward `--exit-code`, in `--json` as `matview_drift`). `--json` for tooling, `--exit-code` (0 in sync / 2 drift / 1 error). Tables + enums (structural) + matview drift; always available (even after release)
- `dbd release` (alias `dbd baseline`) — cut v1: write a baseline snapshot at the current `project.version` and set `project.released: true`, locking in the snapshot/migration workflow (disables `reconcile`). Refuses if already released, snapshots exist, or the design has errors
- `dbd combine` — combine DDL into single SQL file (scope-aware)
- `dbd graph` — dependency graph as JSON (scope-aware)
- `dbd diagram` — build the schema model and open the hosted interactive viewer (model gzip-encoded in the URL fragment, client-side only); `--print-url` prints the link, `--site`/`$DBD_DIAGRAM_URL` overrides the base, `--json -f` writes the raw SchemaModel JSON for upload/tooling
- `dbd dbml` — generate DBML documentation (scope-aware: `--scope` filters to the scope's working set)
- `dbd snapshot` — diff vs latest snapshot, generate migration SQL; smart multi-snapshot splits renames/type-changes/enum-removals into safe stages (with `*.data.sql` corrections)
- `dbd migrate` — show migration status (read-only; `--status`). Pending migrations are run by `dbd apply`, not here
- `dbd policies` — apply RLS policies from `policies/<schema>/<table>.sql` (idempotent, fail-forward)
- `dbd doctor` — audit/migrate config + layout: old-format design.yaml, stale files, and plural DDL folders → singular (`ddl/functions/`→`ddl/function/`; collision keeps newer, backs up older as `.bkp`)
- `dbd reset` — drop the project's own objects entity-level (functions/materialized views/views/tables/sequences/enums, reverse order; matviews `DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW … CASCADE` before the views/tables they read); keeps schemas + extensions by default. `--schemas`/`--extensions`/`--clean` opt into DROP SCHEMA/EXTENSION; `--target <postgres|supabase>` (default `postgres`) sets the protected-schema set. Guarded by _dbd_meta env check; `--scope` restricts to the scope's objects
- `dbd format [--check]` — DDL formatter; river-style SELECT/VIEW bodies on by default (`query_style: river`/`none`, `gutter`); river output is AST-verified and falls back to keyword-case-only if it can't reproduce a query faithfully (CTEs, etc.). `--check` exits 1 if any file would change (drop-in for pre-commit; `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml` ships `dbd-format` + `dbd-format-system`)

Reverse-engineering coverage (`init --from-db`/`merge`): schemas, extensions, enums, tables (columns, defaults, identity, PK/FK/unique/check constraints, indexes incl. gin/gist/brin/hash, comments, serial/identity columns), views, materialized views (definition + indexes from `pg_matviews`, written to `ddl/materialized_view/`), functions & procedures (verbatim), roles (opt-in `--roles`), standalone sequences. Not captured: partial/expression indexes, triggers. A DBML source (`--from-dbml`) = schemas/enums/tables/FKs only. A SQLite source (`--from-db sqlite://…`) = tables/views/user-indexes captured verbatim from `sqlite_master` (CHECK/affinity/AUTOINCREMENT/WITHOUT ROWID preserved; no schemas/enums/functions/sequences/roles; triggers skipped). The reverse dialect (postgres vs sqlite target) is taken from the connection URL scheme.

Global flags: `--scope <name>` selects a `scopes:` entity subset; `--deps report|include` overrides that scope's gap policy for one run. Honored by `inspect`/`apply`/`import`/`deploy`/`reconcile` (gap-gated writes) and `dbml`/`combine`/`graph`/`export`/`reset` (filter-only — they don't gate on gaps; `inspect --scope` is where gaps surface). All filter to the entity working set (`reset` drops those entities; `--schemas` additionally restricts the dropped schemas to the scope's).

## Architecture

- Parser: sqlparser-rs (pure Rust, multi-dialect)
- Adapters (all working):
    - PostgreSQL + Supabase (sqlx, `postgres://`) — COPY streaming import, namespace-aware catalog
    - SQLite (sqlx-sqlite, `sqlite://`/`sqlite::memory:`/`file:`) — batched multi-row INSERT (≤500 rows or 32k binds per batch), trigger-aware DDL splitter, ~150 builtins + `sqlite_*` prefix recognised offline
    - Convex (codegen, `convex:`/`convex://<dir>[?deploy=true]`) — flattens names, maps SQL → `v.*` validators, enums emit `export const X = v.union(v.literal(…))` above `defineSchema`, single-column FKs emit `v.id("table")`; opt-in `npx convex deploy` after apply; `import_data` shells out to `npx convex import` per table
- Classification: adapter-owned — each adapter knows its target's catalog (Postgres queries pg_proc/pg_type, SQLite uses a sorted builtins list + `sqlite_*` prefix rule, Convex defers everything to user-defined)
- Parallel parsing: rayon for CPU-bound file parse, tokio for async DB operations
- Library-first: `dbd-core` crate for embedding, `dbd-cli` for the binary
- Reference cache: `inspect --from-db` snapshots all user-defined entities to `.dbd/refcache.json`; subsequent offline runs consult it to silence "Unresolved reference" warnings without a live DB

## Key types

- `Entity` — central type for all DDL objects
- `TableDef` — parsed table structure (columns, FKs with actions, indexes, constraints, comments)
- `EntityType` — Schema, Extension, Role, Sequence, Enum, Table, View, MaterializedView, Function, Procedure, External, Import, Export
- `DatabaseAdapter` trait — connect, apply (single + batch, incl. transactional begin/commit/rollback batch), import/export, classify_reference, resolve_entity, list_entities, introspect (reverse-engineer), migration + meta tracking
- `RefCache` — JSON snapshot of remote entity names for offline `inspect`

## Safety

- `_dbd_meta` table records environment (dev/prod) and version in the database
- `dbd reset` blocked in prod (always) and in dev after v1 snapshot
- `project.released` (set by `dbd release`) disables the in-place `dbd reconcile` workflow — after release, schema changes must go through snapshots + `dbd apply`
- `dbd reconcile` never touches schemas the design doesn't declare; column drops need `--allow-destructive`, whole-table (orphan) drops need `--prune`
- `--force` overrides safety guards
- For Convex (codegen target) the equivalent state lives in `<output>/.dbd_state.json`
